title: Give screen recording stop more than five seconds to mux
head: 7ce02b929910
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Coordinate the timeout with open IPC-stop PR #10397: its stop replaces the bounded wait with a wait that has no receive timeout
leads.consequence: The branches diverge and an actual three-way merge conflicts at the stop block (merged-10397/result:230-258). If resolved using #10397's stop implementation, OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_STOP_TIMEOUT is never read and the 30-second hard cap disappears: gsr-cli stop deliberately uses GSR_CLI_NO_REPLY_TIMEOUT, and the server replies only after gsr_recorder_run has returned and the recording trailer has been written. A recorder stuck during shutdown can keep the stop invocation waiting without the force-kill notification. Retaining only this PR's stop instead forfeits #10397's IPC-based targeting. Reconcile both behaviours explicitly, or define which supersedes the grace cap.
leads.triage: verified by coordinator in gsr 6.1.3 source (tools/gsr-cli/main.c:18-19,89-96,356-358; src/cli/main.c:497-503) and Opus draft check; published as #10397 bullet

leads.summary: Coordinate the grace-loop predicate and upper bound with open wf-recorder fallback PR #13362
leads.consequence: A three-way merge of divergent #13362 and this head conflicts on the two while-loop lines (merged-13362/result:373-378). #13362 changes both status/stop signalling to an executable-aware process helper that also sees wf-recorder; keeping only this head's pgrep loop either skips its grace period for wf-recorder and immediately enters the other PR's still-live force-kill branch, or, if the script calls this PR's pkill path, does not stop wf-recorder. Keeping #13362's old count<50 loop instead discards the new default and configurable stop grace, force-killing after five seconds. The merged loop must use the helper and max together, and the header must retain both descriptions.
leads.triage: corroboration; Opus adds header conflict, published

leads.summary: Repeated stop invocations can both finalize the same recording
leads.consequence: A second hotkey/bar/menu stop while the recorder is still alive passes screenrecording_active, signals it again and enters the same wait. When it dies, both stop invocations run finalize_recording against the same state file and race over ffmpeg/mv, preview and rm; duplicate success notifications or an empty filename are possible. There is no ownership lock. #11520 proposes a flock guard, and its three-way merge retains the 30-second loop (merged-11520/result:223-291), but #11520 is not part of this head.

leads.summary: Expose the new stop override in user-facing recording configuration, not only in an executable's header
leads.consequence: The new 30-second default and OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_STOP_TIMEOUT=seconds are documented only in bin/omarchy-capture-screenrecording:22-24. The recording manual explains stopping but not the grace period, the FAQ and uwsm env.d template show how to set the sibling recording directory only, and the shipped agent capture guide lists the other screenrecord variables but not the new one. Users cannot discover how to choose a longer deadline to avoid force-killed MP4 trailers or a shorter deadline for stuck recorders without inspecting the executable. Add the variable, default, 1..600 clamp and env.d example at those recording configuration lines.
leads.triage: verified by rg at head (manual/12 and capture.md mention DIR and DEBUG only); not published: low value after F4 was accepted as resolved in review 2

limits: The behavioral matrix used synthetic pgrep/pkill/ffmpeg stubs inside review.py, not a real GPU/compositor or a suspended muxer. It tested stop branch, fallback and signal-selection but cannot measure real trailer flushing or overloaded scheduling.

The full repository snapshot failed closed on an existing absolute symlink config/omarchy/plugins/omacom.elsewhen; the kept recorder and bin-style suites instead passed from an explicitly scoped snapshot (bin/, test/, two default/hypr files). test/cli was evaluated for the changed header by running omarchy capture screenrecording --help and commands --json; the complete CLI suite was not run.

Other PRs' non-conflicting downstream tests were not run on assembled merged source because no actual merge of the two branches was committed; conflict leads H1 and H2 are supported by numbered merge-file conflict markers and upstream dependency source, not an asserted green merged test run.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to [the previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12559#issuecomment-5857689085) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12559#issuecomment-5857705105), checked at head `7ce02b9`.

**Outcome:** **Verified** on `7ce02b9`: the non-ASCII digit abort and both documentation notes from the previous review are resolved, and no regression was found in the tested scope. The concurrent second stop is unchanged and remains deferred by the author.

| Finding | Status on `7ce02b9` |
|---|---|
| Non-ASCII digits pass the check and abort the stop | Resolved |
| Header wording "oversized digit strings" | Resolved: now "more-than-five-digit strings" |
| Description Test section said `08`/`09` are rejected | Resolved: now describes base-10 parsing, clamping and the fallback |
| A second stop during the longer wait runs a concurrent finalize | Still present (deferred by the author; stop code after the parse line unchanged) |
| Leading-zero and very large values, "Closes #12469" scope, `# Env:` header | Still resolved, rechecked on this head |

### Timeout parsing

**Verified:** `^[0123456789]{1,5}$` matched none of the non-ASCII Unicode code points in `C`, `C.UTF-8` or `en_US.UTF-8`. The previous `^[0-9]{1,5}$` matched 1,040 in `en_US.UTF-8`, including characters that are not decimal digits, such as `²` and `½`. Every ASCII digit string of 1 to 5 characters is still accepted and parsed as the same decimal value.

Running the script's stop path with stubs in `en_US.UTF-8`:

| `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_STOP_TIMEOUT` | `2477ae0` | `7ce02b9` |
|---|---|---|
| `３０`, `٣٠`, `3٠` | exit 1 right after SIGINT: no wait, no toast, no finalize | exit 0, 30 s fallback |
| `３０`, stub recorder exits after 80 polls (8 s) | (same abort) | exit 0, "Screen recording saved" |

For all ASCII values, including `08`, `010`, `0600`, `99999`, `100000` and non-numeric input, results were identical on both heads in all three locales. Waits are loop-bound counts from a stubbed `sleep` (iterations × 0.1 s), not wall-clock times. The author's reply matches these results.

### Related open PRs

The previous note on #11520, #13362 and #10397 still applies. Three details for whoever resolves the overlap:

- **#10397:** it calls `gsr-cli ... stop`, which sets no receive timeout for the reply (gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3, `tools/gsr-cli/main.c`). The recorder sends that reply only once it has stopped recording and written the file (`src/cli/main.c`). If that approach replaces this stop loop, the hard cap and the force-kill path go away with it. The combined version then needs to decide whether a cap is still wanted.
- **#13362:** besides the loop line, it also conflicts in the script's `# Env:` header block, so the new `OMARCHY_SCREENRECORD_STOP_TIMEOUT` lines need keeping as well as `max`.
- **#11520:** if the second-stop fix builds on it, note that its lock is a fixed name in `/tmp` (`/tmp/omarchy-screenrecord.lock`). This script's own comment explains why its other state files were moved out of fixed `/tmp` names into `$RUNTIME_DIR`. Putting the lock there too would be consistent. Only #11520's patch text was checked; the effect of a pre-created lock file was not tested.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `7ce02b9` against the previously reviewed `2477ae0` and the base. The script's stop path and its timeout parsing ran in isolated sandboxes on those revisions, with `pgrep`, `pkill`, `sleep`, `ffmpeg` and the notification helpers stubbed. Runs used Bash 5.3 and glibc 2.44 in the `C`, `C.UTF-8` and `en_US.UTF-8` locales. Other locales rely on reading glibc's regex source, not execution. No real recorder, GPU, display or ffmpeg was used, and the repository test suite was not run (its screen recording test exercises only this script's start path). The concurrent second stop was checked by source comparison only this round. Statements about #10397, #11520 and #13362 come from reading their diffs, a textual merge simulation and gpu-screen-recorder 6.1.3 source; none of the merged results was run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical follow-up review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
